chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Al-Ja'fari, who said:

I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'Why did I see you in the presence of Abd al-Rahman ibn Yaqoub?' He said, 'He is my maternal uncle.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is saying a great saying about Allah; He describes Allah, but He cannot be described. So either you sit with him and leave us, or you sit with us and leave him.' I said, 'He says whatever he wishes. What is upon me from him if I do not say what he says?' So Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you not fear that an affliction might descend with him so it would hit all of you together? Do you not know of the one who was from the companions of Musa (peace be upon him), and his father was from the companions of Pharaoh? So when the cavalry of Pharaoh caught up with Musa (peace be upon him), he remained behind from him in order to advise his father, and he was coercing him until they reached a part of the sea, so they both drowned. The news came to Musa (peace be upon him) and he said: 'He is in the Mercy of Allah, but the affliction, when it descends, there is no defence to it from the one who is close to the sinner.'

key_terms.أَصْحَابُ مُوسَى: Companions of Musa (peace be upon him)
key_terms.عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ يَعْقُوبَ: Abd al-Rahman ibn Yaqoub, a prominent companion known for his theological views
key_terms.وَلَا يُوصَفُ: But He cannot be described (in a limited sense)

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of sitting with the sinners according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) warns his companion against excessive familiarity with the 'people of disobedience,' specifically his ungodly maternal uncle, Abd al-Rahman ibn Ya'qub, to avoid shared divine retribution. He illustrates this principle using the Quranic narrative of a companion of Musa (peace be upon him) who stayed behind to admonish his father, resulting in both drowning together; while the father was in mercy, the companion suffered the affliction due to his proximity. This highlights the Shia scholarly concept of 'qaraba' (closeness) as a factor in sharing the consequences of sin, even if one's own status is righteous.
